newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's CNMV files case against Endesa, chairman.
newsitem.headline: Spain's CNMV files case against Endesa, chairman.

text.p: Spain's stock market commission, the CNMV, said on Wednesday that it had filed a suit for "a very serious infraction" against state electricity firm Empresa Nacional de Electricidad (Endesa).
The CNMV said it had also filed a suit against Endesa's chairman Feliciano Fuster and its finance director Jose Luis Palomo.
The CNMV said the case was based on events surrounding Endesa's takeover bid for Sevillana de Electricidad and Fuerzas Electricas de Cataluna (Fecsa).
Endesa bid for the remaining 75 percent of the two regional utilities in November.

News of the possible takeover was published on October 10 in a local financial paper. But Endesa told the CNMV when it made a routine enquiry into the report that it had no plans to bid for the two companies, the CNMV said.
The CNMV then briefly suspended trading in the shares ahead of a statement by the Industry Ministry.
The move surprised Madrid traders because both the ministry and Endesa appeared to ignore the CNMV by not informing it of plans until the night before the public announcement.
The CNMV said it was basing its case on two points of stock market law that say companies must inform the commission of market moving news and must reply to enquiries.
The CNMV has the power to impose a number of sanctions where "serious infractions" are found to have been committed.
Among these include a fine that can range from a minimum of the gross profit obtained from the illegal activities up to a maximum of five times that amount.
The CNMV could also choose to suspend or limit the type or volume of the operation or activities of the company in the stock market for up to five years.
